messages:
support_julie: hitting you all — customer ABC reports huge p95/p99 latency spike on inference API since ~16:30 UTC yesterday. many requests 10-30s, some 502s. they sent sample req_id=rc_8f3a2. can we triage? :frowning:

sara: thanks — do we have any correlation with deploys or scale events around 16:20–16:40?

mike: not that I can see in deploy history. no code deploys. autoscaler did a couple of pod churns in prod at 16:25 but seems normal.

anish: grabbing logs and metrics now. preliminary: large queue length on runtime pool 'gpu-infer-prod-1', concurrency maxed at 200, backlogged queue > 4k for a few minutes. p95 jump aligns.

kevin: ugh. is admission control configured to enqueue beyond limit or to reject?

anish: current admission config: allow_queue=true, queue_depth=10000, max_concurrency=200, timeout=30s. so requests are piling up rather than immediate 429.

sara: that explains p99s then. long queueing time + KV cache warming on some requests. any single worker misbehaving?

anish: one pod (runtime-7) has 95% CPU and high mem, logs show repeated OOM-kill restarts for a model shard. but other pods also saturated. investigating model-specific hotspots.

mike: can you paste the prometheus queries you used?

anish: sure — pulled these: 
```
sum(rate(redwood_runtime_inference_requests_total[1m])) by (pod)
sum(redwood_runtime_admission_queue_length) by (pool)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

support_julie: customer provided curl repro. they send big context (~3k tokens) plus stop sequences. here's a minimal repro header: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Request-ID: rc_8f3a2" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate`

sara: good. next steps: (1) short-term mitigation to restore p95/p99 for the customer and global users, (2) medium-term config changes, (3) follow-up to prevent recurrence.

kevin: for immediate relief we can 1) temporarily reduce admission queue cap and have queue reject at 2s so we fail fast, 2) enable emergency routing of that route to a separate pool with higher concurrency but smaller batch size, 3) scale up pool nodes. which is least risky?

mike: I prefer fail-fast (429) over letting everyone wait. sets realistic backpressure on clients. we should toggle admission to: allow_queue=false or queue_timeout=2s.

anish: I can flip admission policy for pool gpu-infer-prod-1 to reject queues > 2s. applying now. will monitor.

(ops-bot): admission-config-update: pool=gpu-infer-prod-1 allow_queue=false queue_timeout=2s by anish at 1782005200

mike: also scaling worker ASG +2 nodes now. kicking off autoscale job.

(ops-bot): asg-scale: group=pool-gpu-infer-prod-1 desired_capacity +2 by mike at 1782005255

sara: for the specific customer route, let's enable emergency fallback to 'redwood-small-v1' to preserve latency while slightly lowering quality. how do we wire that quickly?

anish: we have a route override mechanism. adding a routing rule: if route==/v1/generate AND client_id==ABC, route to model redwood-small-v1 with concurrency 500, batch_size=1. applying in 30s.

(ops-bot): routing-rule-create: id=tmp-fallback-1782005320 route=/v1/generate client=ABC target_model=redwood-small-v1 by anish

support_julie: customer confirmed degraded-but-working results for fallback, latency dropped to ~400ms p95. they want full traffic but we need to be safe.

kevin: good. medium-term: we need to change admission defaults to fail-fast for public API, set queue_depth smaller (e.g., 200) and ensure autopromote to larger pools only on load-based heuristics. Also consider per-client soft limits to isolate noisy tenants.

sara: Agreed. add to infra board. Also we should disable very large contexts being processed in the slow path — add request size limit or rate-limited long-context path.

mike: on repro — I reproduced locally by sending parallel requests with large context. saw queue climb quickly. sample curl to reproduce load:
```
for i in {1..300}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @big.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
```

anish: logs snippet from runtime-7 around 16:26:
```
2026-03-10T16:26:12Z ERROR inference/runtime.go:412 request=rc_8f3a2 stage=batch execute error: OOM
2026-03-10T16:26:13Z INFO kubelet: Pod runtime-7 restarted (OOMKilled)
2026-03-10T16:26:14Z WARN admission: queue length 4203, oldest=31.4s
```

sara: nice capture. we need two follow-ups: (A) infra change: reduce max queueing and prefer 429; (B) runtime: make batch eviction smarter when mem low, and expose per-pod mem headroom metric; (C) product: rate limit very large inputs or suggest streaming.

kevin: I'll file infra ticket and assign to @anish for config change; @mike take scaling/ASG follow-up; @sara handle product changes + customer comms.

support_julie: putting note in ticket: INC-2026-3482 — customer ABC impacted; temporary fallback in place; working with eng. customer asked for ETA for full restore.

anish: current status: admission tweak applied, routing fallback enabled, ASG scaled +2 — p95 across pool down from 6.1s to 0.9s in last 5m. tail still has few 5–8s due to in-flight jobs but trending down. will keep monitoring.

mike: let's keep on-call looped for 2 hours. if tail doesn't stabilize we'll revert fallback routing and run a rolling restart on runtime replicas (one-by-one) to clear bad memory fragmentation.

sara: thanks team. action items captured in INC-2026-3482 and infra-boards. I'll DM customer with timeline and note that we lowered queueing to fail-fast and provided fallback to a lower-latency model.

support_julie: customer reply: "Thanks, this helps — prefer fast 429s vs multi-second waits. we'll retry with backoff." :thumbsup:

(ops-bot): incident-update: INC-2026-3482 status=mitigated by anish at 1782006890

kevin: postmortem next steps — instrument per-route queue_time histogram, automated detection for sudden queue spikes + auto-fallback rules, and make default admission policy fail-fast for public tier. I'll draft RFC.

sara: closing thread for now. if anything flares reopen.
